patterns.what_worked: Putting the family gate in the PURE engine (rogue_guide.BUILDER_GATED_FAMILIES + builder_candidate_allowed) and keeping the chain in the class gave one source per fact, made the gate testable in the strict no-WoW sandbox, and made the class side a one-line ask. The SoD latch already existed (ERA + the SoD-only Envenom rune known) and only needed to run BEFORE apply_spell_ids so the builder could see it - that reorder was the only non-obvious piece.
patterns.what_was_hard: Two spec readings had to be settled from the corpus itself: (1) Hemorrhage sits BEFORE the dagger Backstab (the bench's chain table lists it, and the corrected TBC APL branch order agrees: Hemorrhage 26864 -> Backstab 26863 -> Mutilate 34413 -> Sinister Strike 26862 - the audit's 'Hemo-Ghostly fallback (26862)' was Sinister Strike); (2) the bench's pin-to-file map put the guide-slot pin in the pure-engine suite, but the guide slot is class-side, so that pin moved to tests/rogue_state.lua and the engine suite carries the pure gate. Residual, already filed: the TBC APL's known-spell (talent) branch is still unmodelled - a TBC client resolves 'Hemorrhage' from its spell table, so it can answer for a character without the talent; closing that needs an id-based known-spell probe, which the TBC name-vs-id rule discourages.
patterns.skill_gap: Proving a chain-order change needs the *prior* corpus evidence, not just the spec text: the corrected id pairing was the only thing that settled Hemorrhage-vs-Backstab. Reading the bench's own audit line against the N1 correction was faster than fetching the APL.

artifacts.note: No bench file written (the corpus correction is the orchestrator's); the trail is in desks/rogue-hemorrhage/journal.md.
